title: What tap dancing brought to the music
summary: Green says tap brought continuity to improvisation as a mixture of two jazzes, around the time swing was fading and the New Shuffle Along introduced Porgy and Bess talent.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Well, what do you feel the tap dancing did to the music? What did it bring to the music?

It brought a greater continuity to the improvisation in music, because it was -- it was like a mixture of two jazzes -- one jazz and another jazz. See, they had composed the jazz song called "New Jazz," you see. That's when swing was beginning to go out, you see. This was after -- some time after the battle of bands. George White had went back to Europe, as I say, the New Shuffle Along introduced a new singer which became Bess and -- "Porgy and Bess," the American operetta, by George Gershwin. So, --
